claims.text: The pre-fix production estimator (bare-Gaussian host-z kernel, global denominator, peak-density completion sky factor), applied to simulated EMRI events injected at h=0.73 against the real GLADE+ catalogue, rails at the upper grid edge h=0.86 with essentially all posterior mass on the edge (edge mass 1.0); the archived full 3375-event run rails at the same edge.
claims.section: Application to GLADE+: de-railing the posterior

claims.text: Restoring only the isotropic 1/(4pi) completion sky marginal flips the rail to the opposite grid edge, h=0.60 with edge mass ~1.0, on identical data -- the predicted fingerprint of two opposing mis-normalizations, one masking the other, and the sign-flip chain the paper presents as its diagnostic heart.
claims.section: Application to GLADE+: de-railing the posterior

claims.text: Either prior-consistent repair de-rails the posterior onto an interior peak at the injected truth on identical data: local_ratio gives MAP 0.73 (mean 0.730, edge mass ~1e-12) and volume_deconv gives MAP 0.73 (mean 0.740, edge mass ~3e-4), measured on a 494-event seed600 subsample over a seven-point grid h in {0.60,...,0.86}; the catalogue-only baseline was never railed (MAP 0.73, mean 0.737).
claims.section: Application to GLADE+: de-railing the posterior

claims.text: On synthetic universes with known truth (clean single-host limit, 120 realizations x 250 events, sigma_z=0.035), the bare-Gaussian kernel carries a rigid MAP bias of -0.024 in h that collapses HPD coverage to 0--3 per cent at every injected truth, while the volume-deconvolved kernel has residual bias -0.002 to -0.003 and coverage close to nominal; the bare-kernel bias scales as sigma_z^2 (-0.0016/-0.0064/-0.023/-0.046 at sigma_z=0.005/0.015/0.035/0.050).
claims.section: Calibration on synthetic universes

claims.text: The railed posterior decomposes into exactly three distinct normalization defects -- (1) Eddington--Malmquist prior inconsistency of the bare photometric host-redshift kernel, (2) a completion-term sky factor evaluated at the peak density of the localization Gaussian instead of its isotropic 1/(4pi) marginal, and (3) an h-dependent tilt of the global selection sum -- all violating one invariant: every population measure counted exactly once, identically in numerator and selection normalization.
claims.section: The normalization pitfall

claims.text: Two prior-consistent estimator repairs are constructed: local_ratio (self-normalized local ratio of sums, numerator and selection denominator over the same localization-ball galaxy set with the same weights and kernel) and volume_deconv (comoving-volume deconvolution of the host-redshift kernel used identically in numerator and denominator); volume_deconv is adopted as the library default for every headline result.
claims.section: Prior-consistent estimators

claims.text: Eddington-in-z law: omitting the population measure from the host-redshift kernel shifts each inferred host redshift by delta_z = sigma_z^2 q(z_g) + O(sigma_z^4) with q = d ln w_pop/dz, and biases the Hubble constant low by Delta_h ~= -K(zbar) sigma_z^2; verified on the single-host synthetic suite with K_meas ~= 17--20, constant to +-8 per cent across a factor 11 in sigma_z^2, consistent with zbar_eff ~= 0.25--0.27 inside the detected population; at GLADE-like z_g=0.05 the expansion parameter exceeds unity and exact quadrature deconvolution replaces the leading-order shift.
claims.section: Volume deconvolution and the Eddington-in-z law
theorem_assumptions: flat LambdaCDM background with Omega_L = 1 - Omega_m
redshift-independent comoving source-frame rate density R(z)
Gaussian photometric-redshift likelihood N(z_g; z, sigma_z^2)
first-order expansion of ln w_pop about z_g valid (sigma_z q(z_g) << 1) for the leading-order form
GW data fix the luminosity distance d_L, so the posterior peaks where the model distance at the assumed host redshift matches the measured one

claims.text: The exact narrow-beam marginal of the coordinate-density Fisher Gaussian over the isotropic sky prior is pbar_GW(u) = (sin theta_hat / 4pi) N(u; 1, Sigma_uu) with the marginal (not conditional) distance-fraction variance, valid to relative error <~1e-5 at the median 0.2 deg^2 localization; the replaced peak-density evaluation over-weights the completion term by 2/(sigma_phi sigma_theta) ~ 1.6e3 (2 deg error) to 1.8e5 (median localization), and a residual missing sin(theta) Jacobian (median 1.15x, mean pi/2) was found by this derivation and corrected.
claims.section: Completion-term sky marginal over the isotropic prior
theorem_assumptions: the GW likelihood is a trivariate Gaussian in the bare coordinates (phi, theta, u)
the Gaussian is a probability density with respect to the coordinate measure dphi dtheta du, not the solid-angle measure
narrow beam: sky-localization widths sigma_phi, sigma_theta << 1 rad and the beam is away from the ecliptic poles
completeness f approximately constant across the GW sky support (for the factorized completion numerator)

claims.text: The global-mode cancellation assumption Sigma_global(h) ~= C beta_G(h) fails on GLADE+: the raw ratio grows by a factor 2.48 over h in [0.60, 0.86], dominated by the expected n_gal ~ h^3 catalogue-density scaling which cancels, but after removing h^3 a smooth monotonic residual tilt of -17.2 per cent end-to-end remains that multiplies the in-catalogue channel of every event coherently; local normalizations are structurally immune and the global mode is excluded from all quoted results.
claims.section: Discrete-sum check of the catalogue selection normalization

claims.text: The earlier 'information starvation' diagnosis of the railed posterior was a misdiagnosis: prior-inconsistent estimators convert photometric scatter into coherent, N-amplified bias -- a property of the estimators, never of the data; three observables (railing vs broadening, bias-growing-as-sigma_z^2 vs width-growing, invariance under estimator repair) discriminate the two failure classes.
claims.section: Why information starvation was a misdiagnosis

claims.text: No published galaxy-catalogue dark-siren pipeline has a known-truth calibration test in the catalogue-information-dominated, sigma_z/z ~ 0.7 regime: the Gray et al. (2020) mock data challenge used zero redshift error, later gwcosmo releases were validated by code-vs-code agreement on real data (which cannot detect common-mode bias), and the width-inflation experiment of Turski et al. was on real data with no injected truth.
claims.section: Relation to existing pipelines

claims.text: From a pinned-version code-and-paper audit of four published pipelines: the rail-producing normalization inconsistency is structurally excluded from gwcosmo by construction; the volume-weighted host-redshift kernel arrived at independently coincides with the published practice of CHIMERA, icarogw, and DarkSirensStat; but the bare-Gaussian kernel is present in gwcosmo by a declaration (catalogue redshift distributions are posteriors) that no code enforces and no catalogue-only test can falsify.
claims.section: Relation to existing pipelines

claims.text: The silent rail under realistic photometric errors -- while calibrating perfectly on spectroscopic-quality validation inputs -- is a field-level hazard for every independently implemented dark-siren pipeline in the LISA / next-generation-detector era; prior-consistent normalization and known-truth coverage tests at photometric width are prerequisites for catalogue dark-siren cosmology.
claims.section: Abstract / Introduction / Conclusions

claims.text: Systematic-error budget: every mechanism capable of railing or coherently tilting the posterior sits in the fixed (repaired, regression-tested) block; after repair the remaining budget is dominated by quoted model-scope choices at or below the few-per-cent level, of which only the fixed Omega_m = 0.2726 fiducial reaches per-cent level (+1.5--3 per cent on H0 if the truth were Planck 0.3153) -- one to two orders of magnitude below the Delta-MAP ~ 0.1 normalization artifacts diagnosed and cured.
claims.section: Systematic-error budget

claims.text: Eddington-in-M: the bare host-mass kernel omits the per-MBH rate prior R_eff(M); under a log-linear expansion the prior-consistent kernel is exactly a shifted Gaussian M_g_eff = M_g(1 + alpha_g sigma_rel^2), but at GLADE+ scatter (median sigma_rel ~ 0.98) the local slope can predict the wrong sign near the rate roll-off, so the implementation moment-matches the exact first moment by per-galaxy quadrature; on the real-data configuration the fix leaves the 1D posterior essentially unchanged, moves the 2D mean from 0.790 to 0.770 toward the injected 0.73, and suppresses grid-edge mass from 0.216 to 0.023.
claims.section: Rate-weighted host-mass prior (Eddington-in-M)
theorem_assumptions: Gaussian mass-measurement likelihood N(M; M_g, sigma_M^2)
log-linear expansion of ln R_eff about M_g (for the exact-shifted-Gaussian form only)
a Gaussian times an exponential tilt is exactly a shifted Gaussian of unchanged width

claims.text: Two-factor ablation on the same 494-event sample: installing the volume kernel consistently on both sides while retaining the global denominator already de-rails the posterior (MAP 0.76, mean 0.755); switching to the local denominator removes the remaining +0.03 (MAP 0.73). Kernel consistency is the de-railing factor; the global-vs-local denominator controls the residual offset, consistent with the -17 per cent global tilt.

claims.text: The volume deconvolution is exactly h-neutral: writing w_pop(z; h) = h^-3 wtilde(z) with wtilde an h-independent shape function, the h^-3 prefactor cancels exactly against the per-galaxy normalization Z_g, so the deconvolution injects no h-dependence into L_cat and the de-railing it produces on GLADE+ cannot be manufactured by the fix itself.
claims.section: Prior-consistent estimators
theorem_assumptions: flat LambdaCDM, so E(z) = H(z)/H0 is independent of h and d_L(z, h) = A(z)/h factorizes
w_pop(z; h) = h^-3 wtilde(z) with wtilde(z) proportional to I^2(z)/[E(z)(1+z)]

claims.text: Gray mapping: the assembled per-event likelihood p_i(h) = [beta_G L_cat + B_num]/D(h) is an exact algebraic rearrangement of the Gray et al. (2020) hypothesis mixture (their eq. 9 with A14/A15/A17/A18/A19 identifications, up to the smooth-completeness rewriting of the magnitude threshold), remaining finite in the complete-catalogue limit f -> 1; the term-by-term audit found no algebraic discrepancy, and every remaining difference is a deliberate documented deviation, the most consequential being the localization-ball selection denominator (nearest published analogue: their eq. A20).

theorem_assumptions: the hypotheses G and Gbar are exhaustive and exclusive
the hard apparent-magnitude threshold of Gray A14/A18 may be rewritten as the smooth per-pixel incompleteness weight 1 - f(z, Omega)
hypothesis weights w_G = beta_G/D and completion likelihood B_num/beta_Gbar as identified from Gray A14--A19

claims.text: SNR-scale caveat: the seed600 sample was selected at the pre-correction SNR scale (missing dt^2 Fourier normalization; code SNR = physical SNR / 10), so it is a physical-SNR >= 200 population of depth z <~ 0.11 with Fisher uncertainties 10x too pessimistic; because the identical inner product enters both event selection and the p_det injection campaign, the dataset remains a self-consistent mock universe and the de-rail estimator comparison is unaffected, while forecast-grade constraints are deferred to Paper B.
